text:
jason: FYI post-deploy synth for /generate-stable is flagging unstable outputs on canary (5% traffic). similarity score variance spiked; failing determinism probes up from ~0.4% -> 3.5%. holding ramp.

deploy-bot: deploy bot: rolling release v8.0.0 -> v8.0.1 at 1854321800, canary 5%. determinism probe suite started 1854321850. recent probe failures: 42/1200 (3.5%).

qa-bot: failing metric: median output-levenshtein increased, and "response_jitter" alert fired. sample diffs stored in s3://releases/v8.0.1/diffs/1854321987.

emma: did we change sampling or temperature defaults? small studio change in release notes mentioned "sampling-stability improvements" but not sure what actually shipped.

ci-bot: pipeline shows commit 7f4e1a2 (release/v8.0.1). diff includes a runtime flag: sampling.stable_seed=true (default enabled in this release) plus a small change to postprocessor hyphen-normalization. no kernel/model quant changes.

jason: interesting. stable_seed=true should *reduce* jitter. maybe the postprocessor change introduced non-determinism (unicode normalization tweak). prefer trying to isolate: 1) flip sampling.stable_seed back to false (quick) vs 2) revert postprocessor via canary-only override. Which is safer?

sre-oncall: recommendation: prefer config override that isolates postprocessor behavior since stable_seed flip changes sampling semantics and could affect quality. Plan A: apply canary override to use postprocessor v1 (pre-change) and re-run determinism synth for 10m. Plan B: if still failing, pin to v8.0.0 for canary and open rollback window.

emma: agree with sre. here's the override payload i'll apply (canary-only):
```
PATCH /internal/configs/overrides
{
  "scope": "canary",
  "postprocessor.variant": "v1",
  "postprocessor.unicode_norm": "NFKC"
}
```
Applying at 1854322030. propagation expected < 45s.

deploy-bot: config override accepted (tx x9c3f). restarting determinism probe runners 1854322060 -> collecting targeted similarity samples 100/min.

qa-bot: focused synth started 1854322065, suite=determinism-short+long. baseline expected fail ~5/1200. current failing rate 2.1% at 2m mark.

jason: good to see drop. can we grab three representative diffs and tokenization traces for triage?

qa-bot: uploaded diffs and token traces to s3 pointer above, also pushed a small report: diffs show majority of remaining failures are whitespace/unicode-normalization differences.

sre-oncall: that points to the postprocessor unicode tweak being the root cause. holding for full 10m window. if failures <0.6% and similarity distribution aligns, we'll resume ramp. else pin to v8.0.0.

ci-bot: note: we can ship a short patch to revert postprocessor change in the next build; config override buys time and avoids full rollback. created ticket ENG-PP-912 to revert with tests.

rachel: i'll prepare a one-line release note update: "temporarily reverted unicode normalization postprocessor during canary due to deterministic probe sensitivity; follow-up patch pending." will notify release-notes and product.

qa-bot: 8m mark metrics: failures 0.3% (4/1200), similarity histogram back within expected bounds. p95/p99 for response_jitter normalized.

sre-oncall: criteria met. releasing hold and resuming ramp to 25% at 1854322587. keep the canary override in place until the patch lands next build.

jason: thank you. leaving this thread as the ops record: postprocessor unicode tweak caused determinism probe regressions -> canary-only postprocessor rollback via config -> synth verified -> hold released. will attach artifacts to release.
